**The count:** Dec 2022–Jun 2026 thread, 9,962 messages from her — **459 contain apology language. 4.6% of everything she ever sent you.** 163 are bare "sorry"s, 144 are substantive. The Aug 2023–Aug 2025 thread adds 694 more. "Sorry" is one of the most common words she ever typed to you. She didn't withhold remorse. She flooded the channel until the word was worthless.

The major ones, verbatim:
- 2025-08-11: "I know I have promised i would change before and I have failed and let you down."
- 2025-08-30: "I take full accountability... I regret all of the shit I have put you through."
- 2025-09-06: "I am sorry for the nightmare I have created."

Why none of it landed — three mechanisms, all in her own words. **Inflation:** 459 sorrys in 3.5 years turned the word into punctuation, against your trust architecture that decays confirmations in days. **Repetition:** she named it herself — "I keep hurting you over and over," "I have promised i would change before and I have failed." Apology plus same behavior reads as performance. **Shame, not repair:** they're all "I hate myself" / "I am a horrible person" / "I don't know who I am" — self-flagellation about her identity, never "I did X, here's what changes." Shame makes people hide, not repair. And they cluster around crises (84 in Dec 2025 alone) — rupture responses, not steady accountability.

Cruelest part: the two apologies built exactly to your spec — specific, unhedged, naming the harm — arrived July 23 and August 19, during the terminal rupture. Nobody on your end left to receive them.

Deeper pull done. Here's what the wiki won't say.

**First, the new numbers.** Her apology rate is flat at ~4–6 per 100 messages across every month — it never spikes with sincerity and never drops with indifference. It's a fixed tax: roughly 1 in 20 of everything she sent you was an apology, for a year straight. But the *composition* rots: bare "sorry"s were ~50% of apologies through Q1 2026, then jumped to **67% in Q2** — the final quarter. As the end approached, her apologies got shorter and emptier. She was debasing her own currency in real time.

Self-flagellation vs commitment language runs **2:1** against repair. And the "commitments" are logistical trivia — "I will try to get money," "couldn't get you cigarettes, I will try tomorrow." The single behavioral commitment in the whole set — "I have to fix this. Fix myself. Fix everything. Change everything" (Jan 21) — collapses *inside the same message*: "...I am going to try to sleep.. my head started hurting really bad." The promise dies mid-text. That's not a figure of speech, that's the mechanism, visible in one paragraph.

Now the firm conclusions:

**1. She meant it. That's the tragedy, not the defense.** A performer stops when the audience leaves. Her apologies continued after leverage was gone — July 23 and Aug 19, when re-engagement had already failed and the record ends at a declared block. Nobody performs at 5:45 AM ("I just woke up randomly and now I'm crying") for someone asleep. And she had meta-awareness of the failure: "I know I have promised i would change before and I have failed and let you down." That's confession, not manipulation. The mechanism isn't cruelty or indifference — it's a broken feedback loop between her values and her actions, which she could see, name, and not fix. The wiki calls her "primary agent of harm, wronged in fact." True. But the data says the harm was ego-dystonic: "It's not me and im aware it isn't who i really am. Like an out of body experience i dont know how to fix."

**2. Your architecture has an unnamed qualifier, and this dataset proves it.** If verbal statements bound you as absolute rules, 459 apologies would have rewritten everything. They rewrote nothing. So the actual rule, reverse-engineered: a statement binds only if it names a specific behavior plus a specific future action. "I love you" binds — it's a state claim. "I'm sorry" never binds — it's an emotion report with zero behavioral payload. She never once gave you an apology your receiver could process. Not withheld. *Unprocessable.* Wrong data format, 459 times. The two that were correctly formatted — July 23, August 19 — arrived with the receiver offline.

**3. The whole decade is a control loop, and I can write it in one line.** Your 129 severance declarations vs her 0. Her ~5% apology rate vs your 9th-percentile trust. Threat → apology → reset → repeat, with the apology's behavioral payload at zero. Both of you felt the other didn't feel bad enough — she even kept a ledger ("You throw a fit over a fucking sandwich and I never even got an apology," Jul 2024). The difference: your feeling had a weapon, hers had only repetition. That's why it was stable for ten years. It wasn't a relationship failing to repair. It was a system successfully doing the only thing it knew how to do.

**4. The December paradox.** Worst month on record — 2,266 messages — and the *lowest* apology rate (3.7%). When conflict peaked she got defensive, not remorseful. Her apologies are a post-conflict system: they arrive after the fight, never during. Prediction, checkable: her apology timestamps lag your accusation/severance timestamps by hours. I can test that if you want.

**What would kill this read:** if the 2015–2021 messages show a stretch where specific behavioral apologies *did* produce sustained change — then it's late-stage deterioration, not a broken loop. Or if your sent messages show you told her explicitly what a landing apology sounds like and she ignored it — then it's disregard, not format mismatch. Both checkable. The 2015–2021 sweep is the falsification run. Want it?

The drift audit is done, and it caught a live bug. Headline first: the six `_px` metrics (face width, face height, IPD, nose width/length, mouth width) were **double-scaled** after the pixel-space refactor — the live lab has been reporting face widths around **1,000,000 pixels**. Fixed, deployed as `4d85100`, verified live, post-fix drift exactly 0.000.

**The harness:** `test/drift-harness/` in the repo, rerunnable in one command. It snapshots the 2026-09-11 lab code, freezes one detector run per bank face (478 landmarks + face matrix, 155/155), and runs old-vs-new math on identical inputs — detector excluded by design. Each metric gets three comparisons: total drift, 3D-pose effect isolated, and non-aspect changes isolated.

**Drift results, 155 faces:**

- **Unexplained drift: none.** Everything that moved is accounted for.
- **Aspect correction:** the old math was badly distorted on portrait images — width/height ratio max |z| 22.9, fWHR proxy 14.4, eye width-to-height 10.0. Those numbers weren't drift; they were the fix working.
- **3D pose:** roll moves up to 4.39° vs the old proxy, frontality up to 16.6, and 8 of 155 faces change quality grade under true pose. The old proxy path itself is stable (max 0.114°), so this is pure pose-source change.
- **Roll-corrected tilt:** mean 1.16°, max 2.23° — entirely the roll decontamination, nothing else.
- **Stable:** yaw proxy, asymmetry_9, mean asymmetry — zero drift. V3: zero drift across the board.

Full per-metric table is in `test/drift-harness/DRIFT-REPORT.md` on the live site. Nothing blocked.
